correctness.rationale: Chen's Theorem 3.3 proof gives finiteness, a nilradical locally free of rank \(r-s\), and a finite étale reduction of rank \(s\). With \(r-s=1\), local freeness plus reducedness of the base forces the nilradical square to vanish. Its multiplication action then factors to an algebra retraction from the reduced finite étale algebra, producing a clopen section. Unique idempotent lifting through the square-zero ideal and the fact that the complementary étale factor annihilates the nilradical yield \(B\cong(A\oplus N)\times C\). The proof is deductive and covers \(s=1\) separately by allowing an empty étale complement.

value.rationale: The claim classifies the entire scheme at the smallest nonreduced defect allowed by Chen's theorem. It converts a one-dimensional nilradical into a geometric splitting law and a sharp obstruction: a connected reduced étale cover of degree greater than one cannot occur with only one unit of scheme-theoretic excess. This identifies a natural boundary case relevant to interpreting constant-fiber families, rather than merely restating the source or computing an arbitrary example.
